# Walter Blythe

## Overview

- **Age:** 11 years old  <sub>[v5 c4 P24](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Walter  <sub>[v5 c17 P8](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0008), [v5 c17 P42](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0042)</sub>

## Appearance

He is considered the most handsome of the Ingleside children, featuring straight black hair and finely modeled features. He possesses dark gray, luminous eyes that express great depth of feeling, though they can make some feel nervous when he gazes intently.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c6 P27](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0027), [v5 c29 P8](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0008)_

## Personality

He is an imaginative, sensitive boy with a deep love for poetry, beauty, and storytelling. He prefers quiet reading and solitary reflection over rough sports or physical fights, which occasionally leads other schoolboys to view him as soft. Despite a dislike of conflict and a sensitive nature that fears physical pain, he harbors a strong sense of honor and will fiercely defend his loved ones when pushed.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c16 P14](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0014), [v5 c16 P25](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0025), [v5 c17 P16](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0016), [v5 c17 P42](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0042), [v5 c29 P8](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0008)_

- Highly imaginative  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c11 P45](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0045)</sub>

## Goals

- To become a poet  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## History

He spent his childhood playing with his siblings and friends in Rainbow Valley, a hollow near Ingleside that he helped name. He frequently read poetry aloud to the local children and shared imaginative stories, often enthralling or terrifying his audience. After being dared by Faith Meredith to ride a pig through the village, he reluctantly complied despite his humiliation. When a fellow student named Dan Reese insulted his mother and Faith, he overcame his fear of physical confrontation and engaged in a fierce fight, emerging victorious and forcing Dan to apologize. Following the encounter, he found the courage to visit the dentist to address a recurring toothache, realizing that anticipation of pain was worse than the pain itself. He also formed a close friendship with the local minister, John Meredith, with whom he shared his thoughts.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P1](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0001), [v5 c8 P12](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0012), [v5 c8 P26](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0026), [v5 c12 P9](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0009), [v5 c12 P25](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0025), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c17 P41](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0041), [v5 c17 P43](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0043), [v5 c17 P46](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0046), [v5 c17 P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)_

## Quotes

> The flower angel’s aren’t. They are a pale misty blue, just like the haze in the valley. Oh, how I wish I could fly. It must be glorious.  <sub>[v5 c3 P22](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0022)</sub>

> I’m not going to be frightened any more, sir. Being frightened of things is worse than the things themselves.  <sub>[v5 c17 P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)</sub>
